Learning together. Empowered for life.
With over 1300 students, strong outcomes and a caring culture, Yateley School is a place where young people are known, challenged and encouraged.
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Yateley School
Learning together - Empowered for life
Welcome to Yateley School. Thank you for visiting our website and I hope it will give you an insight into our vibrant, happy and successful school and a clear sense of our values and ambitions.
Yateley School is a large and highly accomplished centre of excellence, firmly rooted within its local community. Examination results are exemplary and compare favourably both locally and nationally at both GCSE and A-Level. Above all, Yateley School is a dynamic and exceptional place to learn and work.
Nothing online can ever be a substitute for seeing for yourself, so do please get in touch and come and see us in action.
What We Stand For
Six core values guide everything we do at Yateley School, from the classroom to the community.
Ambitious
We have created an environment that supports driven individuals and encourages others to join them in wondering what can be achieved.
Curious
We ask questions, explore ideas and encourage students to think deeply about the world around them.
Tenacious
We keep going when learning is challenging and build the resilience needed to succeed.
Ready
We prepare students to take responsibility, make good choices and approach opportunities with confidence.
Respectful
We treat people with kindness, listen carefully and value every member of our school community.
Safe
We create a caring environment where students feel secure, supported and ready to learn.

Overview
We were pleased to welcome prospective students to our Yateley Sixth Form Open Evening on Thursday 23 October 2025. The evening provided a helpful insight into the opportunities available to students from a wide range of local schools.
During the event, attendees had the opportunity to explore our course offerings, engage with our team, hear student perspectives and learn about the next open evening.
Thinking of Applying for September 2026?Students considering applying for a September 2026 start are encouraged to visit our Sixth Form website for course information, application details, and key dates.
We would like to thank everyone who attended and contributed to a successful evening.
November 2026
Yateley Sixth Form welcomed students to our Taster Day, giving visitors the opportunity to experience life in our Sixth Form community and explore the range of opportunities available.
Sampling Our Courses:Students had the chance to experience a selection of subjects across sciences, arts, and humanities, offering a useful insight into our broad and balanced curriculum.
Meeting Our Teachers:Visitors met members of our teaching team, who shared how they support students to achieve their best and prepare confidently for their next steps.
Exploring Our Sixth Form Facilities:Students toured our Sixth Form facilities, including the dedicated canteen, pool table, games consoles, well-equipped classrooms, Yateley Library, and outdoor spaces.
We would like to thank everyone who attended and contributed to a successful Taster Day.
Welcome...
We're rolling out the welcome mat for our future Year 7 students, and we couldn't be more excited! Yateley School is thrilled to invite Year 6 students from various primary schools to join us for two days of fun, learning, and introductions during our July Induction Days.
🎉 A Taste of Big School: Step into the world of secondary education as you experience what it's like to be a part of Yateley School.
📚 Engaging Lessons: Dive into exciting lessons and discover new subjects that will ignite your ambition, develop your curiosity and give you a new tenacity for learning.
🤝 Make New Friends: Get ready to meet fellow Year 6 students from different primary schools and build friendships for your Yateley School journey.
No Need to Pre-Book:
Pre-booking isn't necessary! Your induction days will be organised through your primary school, so you don't have to worry about registration.

Attendance and Absence
How to report illness, request planned absence, manage appointments and understand the school’s attendance expectations.
Every school day matters
Attendance is important for learning, safeguarding and belonging. A 90% attendance figure means a student is missing around one full day every two weeks, which adds up quickly across Years 7 to 11.
What to include when emailing absence
Your child’s name
Your child’s form
The reason for absence
Attendance matters
Students should attend school as much as possible and be on time to school and lessons. The school aims for whole-school attendance of at least 96%.
If your child is ill
If your child is clearly unwell in the morning, please do not send them to school. Email the attendance team with their name, form, reason for absence and whether they may be absent for more than one day.
Absence and safeguarding
Attendance connects closely to safeguarding. If a student is absent for three or more days, the school may need to complete a safeguarding visit to check they are safe.
Appointments and lateness
If you know in advance that your child will be absent or late for an appointment, please email the attendance team. Students arriving after registration must report to reception.
Medical care in school
If a child is taken ill or has an accident during the day, they will be cared for until a parent can be contacted. Please keep emergency contact details up to date.
Medication
Medication in school requires an Administration of Medicines/Treatment Consent Form. Medicines should be clearly labelled with the child’s name and form and left in the medical room.
Planned absence
Planned absence requests must be made in writing and authorised by the Headteacher. Unauthorised planned absence may result in a fine.
Late arrival
If your child arrives after registration in Period 1 at 8.45am, they must sign a late slip at reception so the school has a record of their presence on site.
Persistent absence
The school classifies attendance of 90% or less as Persistent Absence, and 50% or less as Critical Absence. The school will work with families to improve attendance where needed.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Yateley School
A warm welcome from Mr P German, Headteacher of Yateley School.
I am exceptionally proud of our happy and successful school. An ethos of high standards and high expectations underpins everything that we do. We work hard to create a caring and challenging learning environment where every individual can strive, enjoy and achieve.
I hold a strong belief in the power of education to change children's lives and the right of every child to receive an excellent education. We have superb provision both within and beyond the classroom and we are confident that the preparation for adult life offered at Yateley School is second to none.
The curriculum is broad and engaging and our accomplishments in cultural and sporting activities are truly inspirational. No child is left out and it is a matter of pride for us that whatever a child's need, we can bring both our resources and individual care and attention to bear to ensure that every young person can thrive.
I believe strongly in the limitless potential of all our students, all of whom are valued as individuals and encouraged to develop their talents to the full in a community where achievement is celebrated.
Our large, vibrant and outstanding Sixth Form is an integral part of the school. Together with much valued partnerships with feeder primary schools and Higher Education institutions, education at Yateley is very much a life-long journey in which we are all privileged to play a significant part.
Our aim is to encourage each student to be self-confident, inquiring, tolerant and positive. We pride ourselves in enabling young people to think for themselves, to think deeply and to think about others.
By the time they leave Yateley, we want each student to have class leading qualifications, a true sense of their self-worth and to be of value to society. A child only has one chance at their education. I believe that our school's offer should be exemplary - no excuses.
Our success is your success and I hope you are keen to become part of our story after viewing our website.
Known, challenged and encouraged
Our school culture is built around high expectations, warm relationships and the belief that every young person can achieve something remarkable.
A culture of ambition in lessons, conduct and personal growth.
Students are known as individuals and supported to thrive.
A broad curriculum and wide enrichment beyond the classroom.

Governors
Welcome to the Governors' area. Our governors help shape the strategic direction of Yateley School, support accountability and celebrate the work the school does well.
Welcome to the Governors' area
As Governors of Yateley School, we have a responsibility to make sure the students are getting the best all-round education possible. We do this by looking at results and outcomes, by asking questions, by talking to staff, parents and students and by visiting the school. We can then legitimately challenge the school to do better in areas which are not performing as strongly as they could be. We also love to celebrate the things the school is doing really well.

Admissions
Information for families looking to join Yateley School, including open events, application guidance, admissions policies, appeals and transition resources.
Start the admissions journey
For those looking to join us, we have a range of events available to help you find out more about our offer. You will find booking details for each event below as well as helpful resources including our application guide, how to apply, and our transition booklet.
If you have a question we have not answered, please contact our Admissions Team who would be delighted to help.
Start with the right information
How admissions work
Visiting our school
We welcome parents to visit the school; appointments can be made to see the school in action during the working day. Details of our Open Evening and Open Morning events will be published on our website at the appropriate time of year. For visits at other times, please arrange a school tour by contacting our Transition and Welfare Manager on 01252 879222 or email admissions@yateley.hants.sch.uk.
Main round admissions
Applications for places starting in September 2026 should be made through Hampshire County Council. Full details, closing dates and guidance are at www.hants.gov.uk/admissions. Our 2026/2027 Admission Policy sets out how places will be allocated if the school is oversubscribed. Parents will be notified of the outcome of their application for a place in Year 7 on Monday 2 March 2026.
In-year admissions
In-year admissions are applications for school places made outside the normal admissions round, for example when a family moves home or wishes to change school. If you wish to apply for a place at our school, please complete the in-year application form at www.hants.gov.uk/admissions. If you are unable to apply online, paper copies are available directly from the school office.
How we respond
We aim to notify parents of the outcome of their in-year application in writing within 10 school days, and we will ensure all applicants receive a written response within 15 school days of the application being received. If a place is available, you will be offered one in writing. If we are unable to offer a place, we will write to explain the reasons and provide information about how to appeal.
Appeals
If your application is unsuccessful, you have the right to appeal the decision to an independent appeals panel. Details of the appeals process are available at www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/admissions/guidance/appeals.

Wellbeing and support
Supporting Students with SEND
Every student with SEND deserves high-quality teaching and tailored support that removes barriers to learning and enables them to achieve their best.
Our SEND Team
Our SEND Team: A SENDCO (Assistant Headteacher for SEND), Deputy SENDCO, and Assistant SENDCO lead our approach. Learning coaches are assigned to each year group for continuity and trust. All teachers receive ongoing INSET training in adaptive teaching and "Ordinarily Available Provision" (high-quality approaches that benefit all learners).
How We Support Your Child
Getting Started
If you're concerned your child might have SEND, contact your child's form tutor via admin@yateley.hants.sch.uk, or email the SEND team at send@yateley.hants.sch.uk. We'll listen, meet with you, and plan next steps together.
Identifying Needs
Teachers monitor academic progress, attendance, wellbeing and social development. If a student isn't making expected progress, we first try high-quality, adapted classroom teaching. If progress remains limited, we assess further and involve you and external specialists as needed.
Adaptive Teaching
Your child's subject teachers use flexible grouping, pre-teaching, visual supports, specialist resources and modified delivery to match how your child learns best. This is our first and most important step.
Specialist Interventions
Beyond the classroom: numeracy, literacy and science support; anxiety workshops; social skills groups; ELSA emotional support; therapy dog sessions; study skills; free-time clubs; sensory room access. Students needing more intensive support can access our Hudson Centre for small group teaching.
Progress Reviews
We set clear outcomes and measure progress regularly. SEND plans are reviewed termly with you, your child, and staff. You'll attend annual parents' evenings and additional meetings as needed. Written records are always provided.
No Exclusions
All extracurricular activities, clubs, trips, sports days and productions are open to students with SEND. We make reasonable adjustments to ensure meaningful participation. No student is ever excluded because of SEND or disability.
Transition Support
Between year groups, we place students carefully and share timetables in advance. Moving to Yateley, we create one-page profiles and learning coaches meet you over the summer. Moving on, we advise on work, further education, independence and achieving ambitions.
Funding and Resources
We provide up to £6,000 for specialist equipment and resources. If more is needed, we'll help you apply to the local authority for an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan.
External Agencies
We work with educational psychologists, speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, CAMHS and local authority services, always discussing with you first and explaining what we hope to achieve.
Support and concerns
If You Have Concerns
Contact the Assistant Headteacher (Inclusion/SENDCO) at send@yateley.hants.sch.uk. If your concern is about the SENDCO, contact the Headteacher at admin@yateley.hants.sch.uk. If unresolved, you can access formal complaints, Hampshire's independent disagreement resolution, or Hampshire SENDIASS for free advice.

SEND Overview
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities information for students, parents and carers.
Every student known, included and supported
At Yateley School, we believe that every student deserves the best possible education, regardless of their individual needs. We provide high-quality teaching and tailored support for students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in a welcoming and inclusive environment.
What is SEND?
Students with SEND may have greater difficulty learning than their peers, or may have physical or mental impairments that significantly impact their day-to-day activities.
Identification
We assess needs through classroom observations, regular progress reviews and information from primary schools, families and external professionals where appropriate.
Classroom support
Teachers make reasonable adjustments such as visual aids, additional time, adapted resources and structured routines to help students engage fully with the curriculum.
Interventions
Some students may need extra support, including small-group interventions or time in dedicated Student Support spaces.
SEND FAQs

Ordinarily Available Provision
Ordinarily Available Provision refers to the support strategies and adjustments that are available to all students as part of quality first teaching, without the need for a specific referral or diagnosis. This includes differentiated teaching, in-class support, and access arrangements built into everyday classroom practice.
Examinations
As a centre we offer GCSE, A-Level and BTEC qualifications at KS4 and KS5.If you have any questions in relation to examinations please contact exams@yateley.hants.sch.uk and we will be happy to help with your queries.
Student Support

Departments
Art & Design
A high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design.
Business Studies
Business Studies is a broad subject in the Social Sciences, allowing the in-depth study of a range of specialities such as accountancy, finance, organisation and marketing.
Child Care
Child Care is the study of the physical, social, intellectual and emotional development of the child from conception to the age of five years old. The course provides a basis for further study of Child Development and other related qualifications and could be the starting point for careers in Nursing, Play Therapy or Teaching.
Dance
Dance is a powerful and expressive subject which encourages students to develop their creative, physical, emotional and intellectual capacity. At Yateley School Dance is offered at KS3, 4 and 5. Students can gain qualifications at GCSE and BTEC level.
Design & Technology
Design and technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. Using creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems.
Drama
Drama is a symbolic language used to represent the real world. Art has been used for this purpose for thousands of years.
English
A high-quality education in English will teach pupils to speak and write fluently so that they can communicate their ideas and emotions to others through reading, writing and listening.
Food & Nutrition
Food and nutrition is about how to cook and apply the principles of nutrition and healthy eating. Instilling a love of cooking in pupils opens a door to one of the great expressions of human creativity.
Modern Foreign Languages
Learning a foreign language is a liberation from insularity and provides an opening to other cultures.
Geography
A high-quality geography education should inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives.
History
A high-quality history education will help pupils gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain's past and that of the wider world. It should inspire pupils' curiosity to know more about the past.
ICT & Computing
A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. Computing has deep links with mathematics, science, design and technology.
Mathematics
Mathematics is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment.
Music
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians.
PE & Games
A high-quality physical education curriculum inspires all pupils to succeed and excel in competitive sport and other physically-demanding activities.
PSHE and Citizenship
A high-quality PSHE and Citizenship education helps to provide pupils with the knowledge, skills and understanding to play a responsible and active part in society and make wise, informed choices about their own individual lives.
Religious Studies
Religious Education is a unique subject, which provides a particular perspective on a wide range of issues, stemming from the concepts of faith and commitment that are at the heart of religion.
Science
Science has changed our lives and is vital to the world's future prosperity, and all pupils should be taught essential aspects of the knowledge, methods, processes and uses of science.

My Child at School (MCAS)
MCAS is your real-time window into your child's school life — attendance, grades, homework, reports and more — available 24/7 via the app or web browser.
What is MCAS?
MyChildAtSchool (MCAS) is an online portal for parents that enables them to view their child's performance at school in real-time via the MCAS app or a web browser.
MCAS allows the child's attendance, grades, homework, assessment, exams, timetable, class list, behaviour, reports and announcements to be accessed whenever the parent/carer wants, 24/7. As well as pupil performance data, the portal also provides general information about school, such as the school calendar and any important announcements.
Attendance
See a live view of your child's attendance record, including session marks and absence reasons.
Grades and reports
View assessment grades, progress tracking, school reports and teacher feedback all in one place.
Homework
Keep track of homework set across all subjects, due dates and completion status.
Timetable
View your child's full weekly timetable including room numbers and teacher names.
Behaviour
Monitor achievement points, behaviour records and positive recognition from staff.
Announcements
Receive important school announcements, calendar events and key-date reminders.

BYOD
Bring Your Own Device guidance and the Student Device Programme brochure for families.
Supporting digital learning
BYOD stands for Bring Your Own Device. We believe that students having access to a suitable device can increase access to ICT, support greater personalisation of learning and encourage self-directed learning.
Rationale
When students can bring a suitable device to school, it can improve access to learning technology and help them build digital habits for school and beyond.
Choosing a device
Not all devices are suitable. Some may not work on the school wireless network, and mobile phones do not have large enough screens or separate keyboards.

Celebrating the achievements, ambition and progress of Yateley School students across GCSE, A-Level and Sixth Form pathways.
Proud of every student
We are proud of our students for the resilience, commitment and hard work they have shown. The 2025 results reflect many areas of strength across the curriculum and the dedication of students, staff and families.

Entry and achievement
Strong outcomes across the curriculum
Several subjects achieved particularly strong outcomes, with high proportions of students securing grades 9-5 and 9-7.
We also recognise the excellent performance in CACHE at KS4 and KS5, which continues to be a strength of the school.

Above the national grade 4+ figures
Nationally, outcomes at grade 4+ fell once again in 2025. Yateley School remains above the national figures in both English and Maths.
Pupil Premium
The gap between disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged students has widened slightly compared with last year, though the overall disadvantaged progress score remains one of the stronger results of the past decade.
SEND
The SEN K progress figure is shown as -0.40, though this includes three students educated off-site. Removing those three brings the SEN K figure to around -0.10, with 20 of 35 students achieving positive progress. This reflects strong, targeted in-school provision.
We are proud of all our students for their hard work, ambition and perseverance. While some outcomes dipped slightly compared with the very strong results in 2024, the cohort achieved many successes across a broad and balanced curriculum. We look forward to celebrating their achievements and supporting them as they move on to the next stage of their education, training or employment.

Homework and extended learning
Keeping homework visible and manageable
Satchel:One is an online tool designed to support pupils in managing homework and ensuring it is completed and handed in on time. It also helps parents and teachers monitor students homework effectively.
Homework online
Satchel:One helps students manage homework and helps parents and teachers monitor the work that has been set.
Homework timetable
All students are set homework. Timetables help families keep track of what work is expected each evening.
Working without distractions
Homework is best completed in a calm space. If work is taking much longer or shorter than expected, please let us know.
